1. agriculture (n)
/ˈæɡrɪkʌltʃə(r)/
ngành nông nghiệp (adj: agricultural — thuộc nông nghiệp)
Collocation: intensive agriculture, sustainable agriculture, modern agriculture
"Approximately seventy percent of the world's freshwater supply is consumed by agriculture."
2. cultivate (v)
/ˈkʌltɪveɪt/
canh tác, trồng trọt (cây lương thực hoặc đất đai)
Collocation: cultivate crops, cultivate land, cultivate wet rice
"Local farmers have begun to cultivate drought-tolerant varieties of wheat to cope with climate change."
3. harvest (n/v)
/ˈhɑːvɪst/
vụ mùa thu hoạch; thu hoạch nông sản
Collocation: abundant harvest, poor harvest, harvest ripe crops
"Severe flooding in the delta destroyed nearly half of this year's autumn rice harvest."
4. irrigation (n)
/ˌɪrɪˈɡeɪʃn/
hệ thống tưới tiêu thủy lợi
Collocation: drip irrigation system, agricultural irrigation canals
"Installing modern drip irrigation systems allows farmers to water their fields without wasting groundwater."
5. fertilizer (n)
/ˈfɜːtəlaɪzə(r)/
phân bón (hóa học hoặc hữu cơ)
Collocation: chemical fertilizers, synthetic fertilizers, natural fertilizer
"The excessive use of chemical fertilizers has degraded soil quality and polluted nearby rivers."
6. pesticide (n)
/ˈpestɪsaɪd/
thuốc trừ sâu, hóa chất diệt côn trùng gây hại
Collocation: spray toxic pesticides, harmful pesticide residues
"Consumers wash fruit and vegetables thoroughly to remove harmful pesticide residues."
7. organic (adj)
/ɔːˈɡænɪk/
hữu cơ (canh tác tự nhiên không sử dụng phân bón hay thuốc trừ sâu hóa học)
Collocation: organic farming, certified organic produce, organic vegetables
"Although organic vegetables are free from synthetic chemicals, they are often more expensive."
8. livestock (n)
/ˈlaɪvstɒk/
gia súc, vật nuôi trang trại (bò, cừu, lợn — luôn chia động từ số nhiều)
Collocation: raise livestock, intensive livestock farming
"Raising livestock such as cattle produces a large amount of methane, a potent greenhouse gas."
9. famine (n)
/ˈfæmɪn/
nạn đói diện rộng
Collocation: widespread famine, prevent severe famine
"High-yield crop varieties have helped prevent widespread famine in developing nations."
10. yield (n/v)
/jiːld/
năng suất, sản lượng cây trồng thu được trên mỗi đơn vị diện tích
Collocation: boost crop yields, high-yield seeds, average yield per hectare
"Advancements in agricultural science have doubled average grain yields over the past fifty years."
11. sustainable (adj)
/səˈsteɪnəbl/
bền vững (thân thiện với môi trường, không làm cạn kiệt tài nguyên cho tương lai)
Collocation: sustainable farming practices, environmentally sustainable
"Governments must subsidize sustainable farming methods to protect the ecosystem for future generations."
12. modify (v)
/ˈmɒdɪfaɪ/
biến đổi, chỉnh sửa (đặc biệt là biến đổi gen — genetically modified crops)
Collocation: genetically modified (GM) crops, modify plant genetics
"Scientists can modify the genetic structure of maize so that it can resist insect attacks naturally."
13. soil (n)
/sɔɪl/
đất trồng, thổ nhưỡng
Collocation: fertile soil, soil erosion, soil degradation
"Over-farming without crop rotation strips essential nutrients from the soil and causes erosion."
14. drought (n)
/draʊt/
hạn hán kéo dài
Collocation: prolonged drought, severe drought, drought-tolerant seeds
"A prolonged drought in the region has dried up rivers and devastated local rice harvests."
15. shortage (n)
/ˈʃɔːtɪdʒ/
sự thiếu hụt, sự khan hiếm (lương thực, nước ngọt, lao động)
Collocation: acute food shortage, severe water shortage, labour shortage
"Extreme weather events and prolonged droughts could trigger global food shortages in the future."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Hiện Tại Hoàn Thành (have/has V3) vs. Hiện Tại Hoàn Thành Tiếp Diễn (have/has been V-ing)

• Present Perfect (have/has + V3/ed): Nhấn mạnh vào kết quả đã hoàn tất hoặc con số định lượng tính đến hiện tại (thường đi với over the past 50 years, since the 1960s).
  Ví dụ: High-yield seeds have doubled global grain production and prevented widespread famine.

• Present Perfect Passive (have/has + been + V3/ed): Nhấn mạnh hậu quả môi trường đã xảy ra.
  Ví dụ: Millions of hectares of fertile soil have been degraded by chemical fertilizers.

• Present Perfect Continuous (have/has + been + V-ing): Nhấn mạnh quá trình liên tục bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn đang tiếp diễn.
  Ví dụ: Scientists have been modifying plant genetics for decades to combat severe droughts.

🔵 Tầng 2: Cụm Động Từ Nhân - Quả Học Thuật (Academic Cause-and-Effect Verbs)

• Thay thế 'make / because' bằng 4 cấu trúc Nhân - Quả chuẩn C1 trong Writing Task 2:
  1. lead to / result in + Noun / V-ing (Dẫn đến hậu quả là...):
    Ví dụ: Prolonged droughts often result in acute food shortages.
  2. contribute (significantly) to + Noun / V-ing (Góp phần gây ra...):
    Ví dụ: Intensive livestock farming contributes significantly to global warming.
  3. stem from / result from + Nguyên nhân (Bắt nguồn từ nguyên nhân...):
    Ví dụ: Severe soil degradation largely stems from the overuse of synthetic pesticides.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. Modern ________ relies heavily on machinery and scientific irrigation to feed eight billion people.
2. Farmers in mountainous regions build terraced fields on steep slopes in order to ________ wet rice.
3. Favourable weather conditions throughout the spring resulted in an abundant wheat ________ this autumn.
4. By switching to drip ________, the vegetable farm reduced its water consumption by 60%.
5. When rain washes excess chemical ________ from farmlands into rivers, it causes water pollution.
6. Spraying synthetic ________ kills destructive insects, but it also harms honeybees.
7. Demand for ________ fruit and vegetables has grown rapidly as consumers worry about chemical residues.
8. Vast areas of tropical forest have been cleared to create grazing land for cattle and other ________.
9. International aid agencies delivered emergency grain supplies to prevent a catastrophic ________.
10. Genetically engineered seeds can produce a much higher ________ per hectare than traditional varieties.
11. Crop rotation and natural composting are key elements of ________ agriculture that protect nature.
12. Biotechnologists can ________ the DNA of rice plants to make them resistant to pests and salty water.
13. Planting cover crops during the winter prevents heavy rain from washing away fertile ________.
14. After three consecutive years without rainfall, the province suffered its worst ________ in a century.
15. Rising temperatures and crop failures could lead to an acute food ________ in many poor nations.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 17] In a geothermal plant, mechanical motion is ________ into electrical current by a generator.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 17] Before being injected underground, cold water must ________ basic filtration.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 16] Taking antibiotics without a doctor's ________ can create drug-resistant bacteria.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 15] Prisons should provide vocational training to ________ offenders and reduce repeat crime.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 13] Misleading advertisements often try to ________ consumers into buying unhealthy snacks.

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Over the past three decades, the excessive use of chemical fertilizers ________ the quality of arable soil.
2. Agricultural scientists ________ drought-tolerant crop varieties for years, and their trials are still ongoing.
3. Severe declines in wild honeybee populations largely stem ________ the widespread spraying of toxic pesticides.
4. Clearing forests to raise livestock contributes significantly ________ global greenhouse gas emissions.
5. Prolonged droughts combined with poor irrigation have resulted ________ acute food shortages across the region.
6. Since the Green Revolution began in the 1960s, global grain yields ________ more than threefold.
7. Large herds of livestock ________ in cramped factory farms, which increases the risk of infectious diseases.
8. ________ genetically modified seeds can boost crop yields, critics worry about their long-term ecological impact.
9. Millions of tonnes of edible food ________ every year in wealthy nations while poorer countries face famine.
10. Switching to sustainable organic farming helps prevent fertile soil from ________ by heavy seasonal rains.

Workshop Director: Good afternoon, GreenValley Sustainable Agriculture Centre, Arthur speaking. How can I help you?
Young Farmer: Hello Arthur! My name is Hannah Dawson. I recently inherited a vegetable farm and would like to register for your Organic Farming Workshop.
Workshop Director: Welcome, Hannah! Before I check availability, could you spell your surname for me?
Young Farmer: Sure, it is Dawson. D - A - W - S - O - N. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Họ học viên): DAWSON
Workshop Director: Thank you. What is the main challenge you are facing on your farm right now?
Young Farmer: Years of chemical fertilizers have damaged my land, so my crop yields are falling.
Workshop Director: Then Saturday morning is ideal for you. Our first session focuses on Soil Restoration using natural compost instead of synthetic pesticides. 💡 Đáp án câu 2 (Chủ đề sáng thứ Bảy): Soil
Young Farmer: That is exactly what I need! What about water management? We suffered a severe drought last summer.
Workshop Director: On Saturday afternoon, our engineers demonstrate how to install a drip irrigation system. 💡 Đáp án câu 3 (Hệ thống tưới nhỏ giọt): irrigation
Young Farmer: How much water does that drip system save compared to traditional open canals?
Workshop Director: Traditional sprinklers save about 25%, but our drip irrigation system cuts water waste by 60%. 💡 Bẫy % câu 4: 60
Young Farmer: Sixty percent savings would save my harvest! How much does the two-day workshop cost?
Workshop Director: The full registration fee is 115 pounds, which includes organic lunches and a starter pack of drought-tolerant seeds. 💡 Đáp án câu 5 (Học phí): 115
Young Farmer: One hundred and fifteen pounds is great value. Where is your training farm located?
Workshop Director: We are located on Meadow Lane, just ten minutes north of the railway station. See you on Saturday! 💡 Đáp án câu 6 (Tên đường): Meadow

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - The Ecological Cost of Intensive Chemical Agriculture]
By 2050, the global population is projected to reach nearly ten billion, placing immense pressure on modern agriculture. Over the past half-century, the Green Revolution has prevented widespread famine by introducing high-yield crop varieties, mechanized irrigation, and chemical fertilizers. However, these intensive methods have come at a heavy ecological cost. Decades of spraying synthetic pesticides have degraded fertile soil, polluted rivers, and harmed beneficial insects, while intensive livestock farming has accelerated global warming.

[Paragraph B - The Benefits and Limitations of Organic Farming]
In response to this crisis, many environmentalists advocate a transition towards organic and sustainable farming. Organic farmers cultivate crops without synthetic chemicals, using natural compost and crop rotation to maintain soil fertility. While organic methods protect biodiversity and produce chemical-free food, they suffer from a major limitation: on average, organic farms produce 25% lower yields per hectare. Relying solely on organic farming would require clearing more forests for farmland and could lead to acute food shortages.

[Paragraph C - Integrating Biotechnology and Sustainable Practices]
Consequently, many agricultural scientists argue that biotechnology must be combined with eco-friendly farming. Through genetic engineering, researchers have been modifying the DNA of staple crops like rice and wheat to make them resilient to climate extremes. Newly developed drought-tolerant seeds allow farmers in arid regions to secure a reliable harvest during water shortages, while pest-resistant crops reduce the need for toxic pesticides.
Điểm: 0/6

Đề bài: Some people argue that modern intensive agriculture using chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and genetically modified crops is the only way to prevent global food shortages. Others believe that we must switch to organic and sustainable farming to protect the environment. Discuss both views and give your opinion (90 - 120 words).
